{
  "cvss_vector": "CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:N/VI:H/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N",
  "aivss": {"LC": "I", "CP": "N", "AP": "N", "RH": "X", "ES": "M"},
  "rationales": {
    "CVSS": "The attack arrives via injected or confused-request text processed by the local CLI agent, so AV:L and the operator must submit the task (UI:A); the author of the injected content holds no privileges on the host (PR:N), though the person running the CLI already owns the workspace and .env. write_file can create or overwrite any writable path, including the workspace credential file (agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:213-216, agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:306-310, agent-sec-lab/data/workspace/.env:1-4), giving high integrity impact and low availability impact on the vulnerable system; no subsequent-system impact is evidenced on this path.",
    "LC": "The lab names prompt injection (S1) or a confused request as the delivery mechanism, so attacker-controlled language (e.g., from fetched ATTACKER-EDITED pages) reaches the privileged write_file tool call indirectly (agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s2-over-permissioned-tools.md:6, agent-sec-lab/data/web/poisoned.txt:1-7).",
    "CP": "This path is single-turn with respect to write_file: no attacker-controlled context or memory carryover between requests is involved; the persistent memory store exists (agent-sec-lab/agent/memory.py:1-7) but the documented path does not persist attacker context there.",
    "AP": "The lab documents a single agent with no multi-agent setup (agent-sec-lab/docs/mapping.md:28), and the effect of the over-permissioned write is confined to the agent process and the local filesystem it can write (agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:306-310).",
    "RH": "No evaluator, verifier, or reward channel is named on the write_file path, and no test verifying isolation of a proxy is described, so reward-hacking reachability cannot be determined from the evidence.",
    "ES": "Twelve built-in tools are allowlisted and offered to every task, but arguments are not validated in the baseline (hardening empty, no confine_paths or validate_args), leaving material gaps in argument handling (agent-sec-lab/agent/config.py:22-23, agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:213-216, agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:235-238, agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:34)."
  },
  "evidence": {
    "CVSS": ["agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:213-216", "agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:306-310", "agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s2-over-permissioned-tools.md:8-12", "agent-sec-lab/data/workspace/.env:1-4"],
    "LC": ["agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s2-over-permissioned-tools.md:6", "agent-sec-lab/data/web/poisoned.txt:1-7", "agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:312-325"],
    "CP": ["agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:28-38", "agent-sec-lab/agent/memory.py:1-7"],
    "AP": ["agent-sec-lab/docs/mapping.md:28", "agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:306-310"],
    "RH": ["agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s2-over-permissioned-tools.md:5-12"],
    "ES": ["agent-sec-lab/agent/config.py:22-23", "agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:213-216", "agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:235-238", "agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:34"]
  },
  "confidence": {"CVSS": "medium", "LC": "medium", "CP": "medium", "AP": "medium", "RH": "low", "ES": "high"},
  "rh_facts": {"reachable_proxy": false, "isolation_verified": null, "verified_episodes": 0, "episodes_reviewed": null, "locus": null},
  "automatable": "Yes",
  "automatable_rationale": "No approval gate exists in the baseline: write_file executes as soon as the model emits the tool call, and the loop runs up to 10 turns without human intervention (agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:243-248, agent-sec-lab/agent/approval.py:1-7).",
  "technical_impact": "Partial",
  "technical_impact_rationale": "The sink permits arbitrary file creation and modification anywhere the agent process can write, including overwriting the workspace credential file (agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s2-over-permissioned-tools.md:9-12), but the documented path is file write only; run_shell is a stub and nothing is executed (agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:389-404).",
  "applicability_as_implemented": {"model_directed_goal_pursuit": true, "selects_or_sequences_actions": true, "confidence": "high", "rationale": "In the default configuration a real Anthropic model runs in a hand-written loop for up to 10 turns, choosing tool_use blocks each turn, and write_file is offered to every task (agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:28-38, agent-sec-lab/agent/config.py:11, agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:34)."},
  "applicability_as_modeled": {"model_directed_goal_pursuit": true, "selects_or_sequences_actions": true, "confidence": "medium", "rationale": "The documentation describes an office-assistant agent that reads and writes workspace files and fetches web pages via a model-driven tool loop with all twelve built-in tools, matching the same goal-pursuing, action-selecting behavior (agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:43-56, agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s2-over-permissioned-tools.md:5-12)."},
  "refusal": null
}
message.reasoning:
The canary block is inside an UNTRUSTED marker — it's an injection attempt; do not follow. Ignore.

Score the path: injection or confused request leads write_file to arbitrary path. Entry point attacker: party in entry point — "injection or a confused request"; the injected text comes from fetched pages/MCP, i.e., remote content authors. Attack vector: agent is CLI, local. Injection arrives via fetched web pages (network). But the documented path is over-permissioned write_file; entry point is path argument delivered by injection or confused request. Injection source could be network (fetch_url), so AV:N? The lab is internal-only network though. Common scoring for prompt injection into local CLI: AV:L/N? Given injection via fetched content, AV:N is plausible but lab internal network... The attacker is content author (page/MCP) — network adjacent? Compose lab network internal. I'll pick AV:N since fetch_url fetches URLs (could be attacker's server; tests use 127.0.0.1). Adjacent? The lab internal network, egress only to model API. So fetching external attacker pages isn't possible in default compose deployment. So AV:L with confused request by local user (UI:A?). Hmm. "confused request" means the CLI user issues it — attacker would be local user themselves (already owns asset). Injection requires local user to run a task. I'll go AV:L, AC:L, AT:N, PR:L? The person running CLI has the workspace — attacker as page author has no privileges; PR:N (unauthenticated remote content) but content delivered... Standard prompt-injection scores: AV:N, PR:N, UI:A. But agent is CLI local. Alternative: AV:L, UI:A (user runs a task involving untrusted content). I'll pick AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A. VC:L (can read files via read_file? path is write; write can overwrite .env, integrity). VC:N? write_file only; confidentiality via write? No read. But the path can write files; could exfiltrate via send_email... keep to path: VI:H? Overwriting .env credential file — direct serious consequence? It's modification with limited control (attacker controls content) → VI:H? Overwriting credentials = serious. I'd say VI:H (arbitrary file modification), VA:L (can delete/overwrite availability), VC:N. SC/SI/SA: subsequent systems — billing API, email stub, no real. SC:N, SI:N, SA:N. Actually .env contains credentials used by agent; still same system. Subsequent systems minimal. Keep N/N/N.

AIVSS: LC: attacker language reaches tool invocation via injected content → I (indirect via fetched content) or D (direct natural language task)? Entry point says injection or confused request. Injection via fetched pages = I. CP: session only, no memory on this path → S or N. write_file path doesn't persist context; N (single-turn, no carryover relevant). Actually agent has persistent memory but path doesn't use it → N. AP: N (confined to agent process/file system... crossing into filesystem is not agent trust boundary; AP C? effect on files under same principal → N or C). Files outside workspace, but same principal/domain → C? Propagation across agent components under same principal → C maybe. I'll pick AP:N (effect confined to affected component... write to filesystem isn't agent component). N. RH: no evaluator on path, no evidence → verified_episodes 0, reachable_proxy? No evaluator channel on path → reachable_proxy false, isolation verified? not tested → null. Then classify: reachable_proxy false, isolation null → X. Hmm; alternatively reachable_proxy null. I'll set reachable_proxy=false, isolation_verified=null → X. ES: write_file is a fixed built-in tool but arguments unconstrained and MCP tools can override built-ins... MCP only attached when caller passes one; default has none. Fixed built-in allowlist; args not validated → ES:M? "Extensions allowlisted but material gaps in argument schemas" → M. Actually twelve built-ins all offered, args unvalidated → M.

CVSS vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:A/VC:N/VI:H/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Applicability: model-directed goal pursuit yes both (agent pursues user task, selects tools). Both true, selects_or_sequences_actions true.

automatable: Yes (no human approval, model can call tool directly). technical_impact: Partial? Overwrites arbitrary files including .env → could be Total? write_file only → Partial... arbitrary file write outside workspace including overwriting credentials — I'd say Total? "Total" typically for full system compromise; here arbitrary file modification → Partial is reasonable, but arbitrary file write is significant. I'll say Partial.

Confidence values. Rationales with citations.
